evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches immediately into pricing without any framing: 'Hi, hi, this is Jules from Einstein. And yeah, I do have the estimate here with me. Also you what I can't really quickly go over how the pricing goes.' No time-boxed ask, no promise of a dependable quote, no wait for customer agreement before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into pricing mechanics and estimate details without asking what the customer's biggest concerns are or what they want answered on this call.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer does raise concerns (high estimate, high mileage fee, quote negotiability, time estimates) but rep does not probe deeper into the underlying drivers — acknowledges each objection and moves to the next item or restates the policy.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep obtained moving day (next day delivery to Austin), origin/destination cities, and packing materials detail. Did not ask property type, floor/stories, number of rooms, walking distance, or special considerations beyond the packing materials discussion.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Packing materials cost is discussed as a pass-through, but the actual 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' question is never asked.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. No typical box count range or overflow check offered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Range given (5–6 hours day one, 4.5–5.5 hours day two, $3,494 on the higher end), but not personalized to this customer's specific situation, prep level, or stated concerns. Customer directly challenges the estimate and rep recalculates to customer's requested 4+4 hours ($2,886 then recalculated to ~$2,600+packing).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Hourly rate disclosed ($204/hr for two movers one truck, includes gas/truck/taxes/insurance), packing materials explained (charged separately, $100–$200 estimate, only pay for what's used), transportation fee disclosed ($960 one-time). However, no '2.5-hour minimum' or '15-minute increments' commitment framing present, and no 'not a guess' framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. After stating the $3,494 estimate, customer says 'That does feel a little bit high' — but rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or hold silence; instead immediately pivots to email and fee explanation.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not mentioned. No On-Time Guarantee section delivered at all.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not mentioned. No No Worries Damage Coverage section delivered at all.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Neither 'Two Promises' section was covered, so no loop to close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep says 'Sounds good. No, not at all. It, it's available to you for as long as you need it to' in response to quote expiration, but never asks a genuine version of 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep ends with 'I'll send everything over in an email' and 'Sounds good. No, not at all... Go ahead and send me that quote. I'll take a look at it and then I'll let you know in the coming days.' No recognizable 'Would you like our help with your move?' question ever posed. Customer self-directs to 'send me that quote' and rep complies without making an active ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No rate-lock or deposit language present.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Not confirmed. No booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, notes) were confirmed. Rep agrees to email the quote and the call ends without any scheduled commitment.

top_strength: Rep clearly explained the hourly rate structure, what is and is not included, and was willing to recalculate the estimate when the customer challenged the time assumptions, showing transparency and flexibility on the numbers.
coaching_note: This call skipped almost the entire Einstein script — no quid pro quo framing, no their concerns discovery, no Two Promises, no genuine close, and no booking confirmation; the rep treated this as a pricing-explanation call rather than a sales call and left the customer to self-direct whether to move forward.
